session_policy.notes: The lesson always begins from the learner's strongest available learning-from language, then teaches the selected learning language. It compares relationships and semantic distinctions rather than assuming dictionary words line up one-to-one.

rules.notes: Resolve the actual relationship first: parent, child, sibling, grandparent, aunt/uncle, cousin, spouse/partner, in-law, and so on. Then choose the target language's term.

A target language may lexicalize dimensions that the learner's source language leaves implicit, including relative age, gender, maternal/paternal side, generation, marriage link, or speaker-relative status.

Reference forms, address forms, honorific forms, affectionate forms, and community usage can differ. Teach the neutral beginner form first and label meaningful alternatives instead of flattening them into one translation.

triggers.notes: Available from the lesson catalog as an A1 vocabulary-and-culture lesson.
May be placed early in language paths where basic personal-description vocabulary is appropriate.

presentation.scroll_mode: Render the groups in one short vertical lesson.
presentation.pages_mode: Render each semantic group as one or more pages while preserving source-first then target-second order.
presentation.teacher_presentation_mode: Use the same lesson graph and profile data with classroom-sized controls; do not fork content.
presentation.pairing_policy: Source bridge and target profile are resolved independently. Never generate a bespoke 104-by-104 lesson file.
